svg.text: Top view. Breadboard rows 15 to 55 are empty and not drawn.
Only one pin row of the ESP32 is plugged in:
3V3 ... D23 into column A, rows 0 to 14.
The other pin row hangs free. Nothing is wired to it.
Pins used: GND (row 1) and D4 = GPIO4 (row 4).
Red dashed pair E58 and F60
Wire 2: D4 strip (B4) to hole A58
Wire 1: GND strip (B1) to hole J60
USB data cable: ESP32 micro-USB to laptop
Two legs on the same side of a button are always joined inside it.
Diagonal legs (E58 and F60) are never joined until you press.
So the button can never short D4 to GND, even if you turn it.
Holes A to E in one row are joined. F to J in one row are joined.
MOVING THE BUTTON? KEEP THESE 3 RULES
1. The button must straddle the centre groove (two legs above it, two below).
2. The D4 wire and the GND wire go in different rows AND different halves (A to E, and F to J).
3. Stay in rows 16 and higher. Rows 0 to 14 belong to the ESP32 pins.
